accept.reason: Reframes learning with noisy labels as distilling a compact clean support set, sidestepping explicit per-sample noise estimation; links the memorization literature (common patterns learned first) to what dataset distillation synthesizes.

Covers the three main dataset-distillation families (parameter matching DATM, distribution matching DANCE, meta-learning RCIG) on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet, symmetric noise rates 0.2-0.8 and a sweep over IPC.
Striking headline: at high symmetric noise a single distilled image per class beats training on the full noisy dataset.
accept.location: Section 4, Observation-I text ("a single distilled sample per class surpasses the baseline"); Figure 2(a)

accept.reason: Reports an informative negative result: structured asymmetric noise is absorbed into the distilled data, and only DATM matches the full-data baseline at tau in {0.2, 0.4} with large synthetic sets.
Includes human-annotation noise (CIFAR-10N Aggre/Random/Worst, CIFAR-100N fine) with the noise rates stated.
Identifies a noise-rate/IPC trade-off: distillation helps at high noise but underperforms at low noise (Aggre) because clean information is lossily compressed.
Noise models and the three distillation objectives are formally stated, so the setting is easy to follow.
Visualizes DATM distilled images on CIFAR-10 at tau 0.0-0.8, said to retain discriminative features under high noise.
Practical angle: a small distilled set can be shared offline instead of raw data, which the paper argues suits high-privacy settings with noisy data.
Uses public benchmarks and published distillation methods under their original evaluation protocols with standard ConvNet backbones.
accept.location: Section 4 Implementations ("following the evaluation protocols of DATM, DANCE, and RCIG")

accept.reason: Raises a concrete open question with follow-up value: how much to distill given the noise level, and whether distillation can estimate the noise rate.

reject.reason: No learning-with-noisy-labels method is compared. The only reference point is cross-entropy training on the full noisy dataset, so 'good label denoisers' is shown against the weakest possible baseline, not against the methods (co-teaching, DivideMix, etc.) the paper itself cites.
reject.location: Section 4 Observation-I ("over the baseline trained on the entire noisy dataset"); Figures 2, 4, 5 captions; [14], [24] cited only in Sections 1-2
reject.fix: Add at least co-teaching, DivideMix and one transition-matrix or robust-loss method on the same ConvNet and data, plus the field-standard ResNet setting; about 1-2 GPU-weeks on CIFAR scale.

reject.reason: The full-data baseline's protocol (architecture, epochs, early stopping, augmentation) is not stated, and the obvious controls at matched budget are missing: early-stopped CE, a random subset and a coreset of IPC samples per class. Without them the gain cannot be attributed to distillation rather than to fewer noisy samples or early stopping.
reject.location: Section 4 Experiment-I ("We use Cross-Entropy loss by default"); Figure 2 caption (dashed lines = full dataset)
reject.fix: State the baseline protocol; add early-stopped CE and random/coreset subsets at each IPC; cheap (hours per configuration).

reject.reason: The proposed mechanism (distillation captures common patterns and ignores noise) is asserted, not tested. A competing explanation is that matching early expert trajectories (DATM) or using early-trained encoders (DANCE) inherits the early-learning phase before memorization; no ablation on expert epochs, trajectory range or label handling separates the two.
reject.location: Section 4 Insight-I ("the distillation process primarily captures common patterns"); Section 3.2 Benchmark-I/II
reject.fix: Ablate expert trajectory range / expert training epochs under noise and report label quality of what is matched; moderate cost.

reject.reason: Corollary-II contradicts the paper's own results. Eq. 11 asserts tau >= 1 - C*IPC/|S|; for CIFAR-10 with IPC=1 this gives tau >= 0.9998, yet Observation-I reports that IPC=1 already surpasses the full-data baseline at tau=0.6. For CIFAR-100N with IPC<10 it gives tau >= 0.98 versus the stated 40.20%. Rearranging Eq. 10 gives the opposite inequality, tau <= 1 - C*IPC/|S|.
reject.location: Section 4, Corollary-I (Eq. 10), Corollary-II (Eq. 11), Observation-I and Observation-III text
reject.fix: Remove or correct Corollary-II and derive it formally; no compute.

reject.reason: Both corollaries are stated without proof or assumptions; delta in Eq. 11 is never defined, and 'perfectly preserve the sample information' is undefined. Eq. 10 reduces to the count of clean samples per class, which carries no information about distillation.
reject.location: Section 4, Corollary-I (Eq. 10) and Corollary-II (Eq. 11)
reject.fix: Provide definitions, assumptions and proofs, or recast as heuristics; no compute.

reject.reason: No seeds, number of runs, variance or numeric tables; every result is a curve in a figure, and the text uses 'significantly outperform' and 'consistently' with no test. CIFAR-scale experiments are cheap enough that multiple seeds are expected.
reject.location: Section 4 Observation-I ("significantly outperform the baseline"); Figures 2, 4, 5 captions (only solid and dashed lines described)
reject.fix: Report mean +/- std over >=3 seeds in tables for each dataset/noise/IPC; a few GPU-days.

reject.reason: Title says 'In the Wild', but the only real-noise data are CIFAR-10N/100N (32x32). Clothing1M and WebVision are introduced as classic real-noise benchmarks and never evaluated.
reject.location: Title; Section 3.1 Natural Noise ("Clothing1M [48] and WebVision [27]"); Section 4 Experiment-III
reject.fix: Evaluate on Clothing1M or (mini-)WebVision, or retitle and narrow the claim; costly for distillation at that scale.

reject.reason: 'Enhances training efficiency' is never measured. Distillation itself (expert trajectories, bi-level or matching optimization) is expensive and its cost is not reported against simply training a robust model.
reject.location: Abstract ("enhances training efficiency"); Contributions bullet 1; Section 5
reject.fix: Report end-to-end GPU hours (expert training + distillation + evaluation) versus baselines, or drop the claim.

reject.reason: 'Strong privacy protection' is asserted with no threat model, attack or analysis; whether distilled data protect privacy is contested in the dataset-condensation privacy literature, which is not cited.
reject.location: Abstract ("providing strong privacy protection through offline processing"); Section 5
reject.fix: Run a membership-inference evaluation on the distilled sets or remove the claim; cite the condensation-privacy debate.

reject.reason: The tail-class / imbalanced-data finding appears in the abstract and contributions, but the body only hypothesizes it; no imbalanced experiment is run.
reject.location: Abstract; Contributions bullet 3; Section 4 Insight-II ("We further hypothesize that challenging clean samples")
reject.fix: Add a long-tailed CIFAR experiment with noise, or state it as a hypothesis in abstract and contributions.

reject.reason: The 'vicious cycle' of noise-evaluation methods is argued but never demonstrated, and distillation does not escape noise evaluation: the paper concedes the IPC must be chosen according to the unknown noise level.
reject.location: Section 1 Status Quo; Section 1 ("the relationship between the amount of data to be distilled and the level of noise remains an open question"); Section 4 Insight-I, Insight-III
reject.fix: Show the cycle failing in an existing method, and give an IPC-selection rule that needs no noise estimate, or tone down.

reject.reason: No new method; the contribution is a benchmark of three existing distillers. Cross-field prior art in data selection already studies selecting a small clean-dominated subset under label noise (coresets for robust training), and early-learning before memorization is well known; neither selection-based work is cited or compared. Basis: from memory, no literature search ran [verify].
reject.location: Section 1 Contributions; Section 2.1; reference list (no coreset or data-selection-under-noise work)
reject.fix: Position against coreset/data-pruning methods for noisy labels and compare at matched subset size.

reject.reason: Coverage is uneven: asymmetric noise only on CIFAR-10/100 (no Tiny-ImageNet) and only a few rates; natural noise only on CIFAR-N.
reject.location: Section 4 Experiment-II; Figure 4 caption
reject.fix: Add Tiny-ImageNet asymmetric runs; low cost.

reject.reason: Figure captions say 'validation performance' while the text says test accuracy is reported 'throughout the distillation process'; if the plotted value is the best test accuracy over distillation iterations, model selection is on the test set.
reject.location: Figure 2/4 captions ("The validation performance"); Section 4 Implementations ("Final test accuracies are reported throughout the distillation process")
reject.fix: State which split selects the distillation checkpoint and report on a held-out test split.

reject.reason: No distillation hyperparameters (iterations, learning rates, synthetic-label settings), no expert-training details under noise, no compute, no code statement.
reject.location: Section 4 Implementations (only backbones and protocols named)
reject.fix: Add an implementation appendix and release code; no compute.

reject.reason: It is not stated whether DATM experts are trained on the noisy labels, how real images are grouped per class (by noisy label), or whether DATM's soft labels come from noisy experts; these decide where denoising can happen.
reject.location: Section 3.2 Benchmark-I; Section 4 Implementations
reject.fix: Specify the noisy-data pipeline for each method.

reject.reason: Presentation slips: 'Realted Works', 'bellow', 'Both of which' for three noise types, Eq. 4 uses step N while the text defines T steps; about two pages re-describe existing methods while results get about two.
reject.location: Section 2 heading; Section 1 Contributions; Section 3.1 Noise Type; Section 3.2 Eq. 4
reject.fix: Proofread; move method recaps to an appendix and add result tables.

reject.reason: The layout (Figure 1 beside the abstract, CVF-style numbered headings) looks like a CVPR-style template rather than the ICLR template; cannot be confirmed from extracted text.
reject.location: Page 1 layout; Section headings
reject.fix: Use the ICLR 2026 template.

reject.reason: Contribution check Q1/Q3: the insights are largely expected (symmetric noise averages out, structured noise is learned as a pattern), as the paper itself says for Observation-II; the delta is a re-run of existing methods on noisy CIFAR variants.
reject.location: Section 4 ("This phenomenon is consistent with intuition"); Insight-I, Insight-II
reject.fix: Provide a non-obvious finding: e.g. which distillation family is robust and why, or a method that fixes the asymmetric failure.

reject.reason: Contribution check Q4: conclusions hold only in the high-noise regime; at realistic low noise (Aggre 9.03%) distillation underperforms the full noisy data, and accuracy ceilings of ConvNet-trained distilled sets are far below standard noisy-label results, so practitioners gain little.
reject.location: Section 4 Observation-III ("these distillation approaches struggle to perform well"); Insight-III
reject.fix: Show a regime where distillation beats strong noisy-label methods at realistic noise, or reframe as an analysis of distillation robustness.

reject.reason: Only 3/4-layer ConvNets are used for distillation and evaluation; no cross-architecture evaluation, so it is unknown whether the 'denoised' sets help models practitioners train.
reject.location: Section 4 Implementations ("a simple ConvNet [40] architecture")
reject.fix: Evaluate distilled sets on ResNet-18 and compare with noisy-label methods on that backbone; moderate cost.

reject.reason: The 'denoiser' claim is measured only through downstream accuracy; there is no direct measure of what the distilled set contains (e.g. label agreement of a clean-trained classifier on the synthetic images, or per-class confusion inherited from asymmetric flips).
reject.location: Section 4 Observations I-III; Figure 3 (qualitative only)
reject.fix: Classify synthetic images with a clean-trained model and report agreement with their labels per noise rate; cheap.

answered.reason: DATM does not scale and would be infeasible at Tiny-ImageNet scale.
answered.answered_at: Section 3.2: the memory-efficient variant of Cui et al. [9] is used ("Unless otherwise specified, Benchmark-I referenced later denotes this accelerated version").

answered.reason: Only synthetic label noise is studied.
answered.answered_at: Section 4 Experiment-III and Figure 5: CIFAR-10N and CIFAR-100N human annotations (the scale concern remains as R7).

answered.reason: Distillation methods are run outside their published protocols.

Section 4 Observation-II/Insight-II (asymmetric failure) and Observation-III/Insight-III (low-noise underperformance).
